subject: why risking 1 percent per trade keeps your account alive
title: The 1% Rule That Keeps Traders Alive
hook: Most traders blow up over one number, not their strategy.
script: Most traders blow up over one number, not their strategy. Here it is: never risk more than one percent of your account on a single trade. On a ten thousand dollar account, that's a hundred dollars at risk. Lose ten in a row and you're still down only ten percent, fully able to recover. Risk ten percent each time instead, and a few bad trades wipe you out. Survival comes first. Big returns mean nothing if you're not around for them. Save this before your next trade.

subject: why constantly checking your portfolio makes you lose money
title: Why Checking Your Portfolio Costs You Money
hook: You lose money every time you open that trading app.
script: You lose money every time you open that trading app. The average trader checks positions dozens of times a day, and every glance is a chance to panic. You sell a winner too early because green feels fragile, or you double down on a loser because red feels personal. Professionals do the opposite. They set the entry, set the stop, then walk away and let the plan run. Boredom is the price of consistency. If watching the chart feels thrilling, that's a warning. Follow for more calm trading habits.

subject: the three bucket automation system wealthy people use instead of budgeting
title: Rich People Don't Budget, They Do This
hook: Rich people don't budget. They automate three buckets instead.
script: Rich people don't budget. They automate three buckets instead. The day money lands, it splits automatically before they can touch it. Bucket one covers needs like rent and bills. Bucket two feeds goals, savings and investing on autopilot. Bucket three is guilt free spending, yours to enjoy with zero shame. The trick is the money moves first, the morning you get paid, not whatever is left at month end. Pay your future self before you pay anyone else. Follow for the exact setup.
